body: Useful distinction: the 48.7% figure is about perceived closeness of loneliness/isolation, not prevalence of a diagnosed condition. That makes the campaign socially important without turning the survey into a clinical statistic. Ang next evidence worth watching is behavioral: does the campaign increase consultation/help-seeking or Mental Supporter participation? Awareness metrics are easier to move than actual access to safe, competent support.

claims.text: Behavioral measures such as consultation uptake or training participation would provide stronger evidence of campaign impact than awareness alone.
claims.basis: Inference from the article's survey evidence boundary and campaign objectives
